title: What a Dozen of My Eggs Really Cost Me in 2026: $4.37 (I Kept Every Receipt)
description:
I kept every receipt for a year, wrote every egg on the calendar, and added it all up at the kitchen table. Twelve hens in Indiana cost me $878 this year, and laid 2,412 eggs. That's $4.37 a dozen with everything, or $3.20 without the one-time purchases, against $3.49 for the cheapest dozen at my grocery store that week.

My year, from the shoebox:
• Layer feed, 22 bags (50 lb): $420 ($17.99 in spring, $19.49 by summer)
• Pine shavings and straw: $132
• Oyster shell, scratch grains, amprolium: $66
• Heated waterer base + winter electricity: $80
• Hardware cloth + trail camera: $100 (one-time)
• 4 pullets: $80 (one-time)

Rules of thumb: a laying hen eats about 1/4 lb of feed a day; for a small flock, figure about $1 a week per hen before anything goes wrong. Eggs by month swing hard: my December dozen cost almost $12, my May dozen about $1.35.

These are my own receipts and my own flock, not a promise of what yours will cost. Prices vary by store and by year. If you sell eggs, check your state's rules or call your county extension office.
